doc.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

chapter: The Tonight Show and famous accompaniments
title: Accompanying Marilyn Horne
summary: Faded sheet music and Doc turning pages caused Smith to fake an aria behind Marilyn Horne.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: experiences. It was great as a pianist, I mean once a wonderful lady, an opera singer, Marilyn Horne came on. And you know, so we had a rehearsal, a very fading piece of music, a yellowing piece of music, and just like you described with the flycrap. And so I’m just playing it. And you know I’ll read anything. And I’m playing it, but you don’t have the feeling. You’ve got to be born to that kind of music like I’m born to play jazz. But I’m reading and I’m reading. And we’re going on. And so fine, we get to the show, so again, they put the piano out in the center. Now she comes out and she’s got these wonderful parts, what a wonderful singer. And we’re playing and we’re playing and playing. And Doc is turning pages for me. So Doc got nervous, and he turned several pages at once, and there I am trying to fake some aria which I have no idea what it’s about. And you can’t really fake that stuff. I mean it sounds like free jazz. And this lady is singing her heart out. But anyway, somehow we got back on track but then I noticed after that that the lady brought in her own accompanist the next time she came in.
That must have been, that must have been a blast. Tell me some of the other interesting people that you accompanied when you played on the show.
